• Open Shortcuts app
• Click "+" for new shortcut
• Name it "Lectio Divina DND On"

• Select Focus mode (e.g. "Do Not Disturb")

• Save shortcut

• Save shortcut

intro_pages.title: Introduction
intro_pages.section1:
Dear friends!

Wherever we are in life, the Holy Spirit invites us into an active friendship with Christ - the Word that became flesh and came to dwell among us (John 1:14). If we want to build a friendship with Christ, we need to learn to listen to Him, to perceive what God wants to tell us. One of the best ways to listen to God is to read His Word regularly.
intro_pages.section2: That is why we want to offer you an ancient way to read God's Word fruitfully and apply it to your life. It is called "Lectio Divina", which literally means "divine reading" but is also translated as "spiritual reading".
intro_pages.section3:
Lectio Divina has been known since the first centuries of the Church. Origen used the Greek phrase thea anagnosis (divine reading) to describe the way to approach God and His will through Scripture.

This practice became common when the desert fathers and mothers made God's Word the basis of their personal prayer. Shortly afterward St. Benedict made Lectio divina the basic rule of Western monasticism. From the earliest centuries to today, Lectio Divina remains a living practice inviting us into an intimate relationship with God.
intro_pages.section4: In 2005 Pope Benedict XVI emphasized that one of the effective ways for the Church to be renewed today is precisely Lectio divina. He said that 'continual reading of Sacred Scripture accompanied by prayer will bring the Church a new spiritual spring.' He clarified this idea by saying: 'Among the many fruits of this new biblical spring I would like to mention the spread of the ancient practice of lectio divina, the spiritual reading of Sacred Scripture. This practice consists in lingering over a biblical text, re-reading it repeatedly, almost chewing it, in order to extract the sap that nourishes meditation and contemplation and becomes life-giving for everyday life. The condition for practicing Lectio divina is that mind and heart are enlightened by the Holy Spirit, the very inspirer of Scripture, and therefore disposed to a posture of reverent listening. This was the typical attitude of the Virgin Mary, symbolically presented in the icons of the Annunciation. It is enough for us to allow the Holy Spirit to lead us - just as Mary did.'
intro_pages.section5: The psalmist confesses: 'Your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path' (Ps 119:105). God's Word can also be a light for us so that we see where to walk in this time of confusion and disorientation.
intro_pages.section6:
That is why we want to offer you this journal. Besides the calendar and space for notes, you will find a notebook where you can write down your thoughts. Later these thoughts can help you find answers to life's questions.

In the calendar section you will find the liturgical references to the Gospel of the day. This can help you choose the text for reading and meditation. We also offer you the website www.lectio.one and the mobile app Lectio Divina, which you will find in the App Store or Play Store.

In the mobile app you will find prepared texts that will help you enter this practice. We regularly add Sunday liturgical readings of the Gospel together with meditation, prayer, contemplation, and a simple call to apply God's Word in everyday life. You can also create your own notes that will be ordered by the meditation date. If you use this option, we recommend naming the note after the text you meditate on or a keyword capturing what you reflected on. This makes it easier to return to the Word you meditated on when you look for an answer to a life question.

how.title: How should I proceed?
how.intro: Reading the Bible with the "lectio divina" method – explanation of the steps:

lectio.title: LECTIO – READING
lectio.body: Read a selected text, for example according to the plan for each day. Read slowly, unhurriedly, prayerfully, aloud, and then again at least three times. Let the text act on you; do not try to grasp it only intellectually. Pay attention especially to the words, phrases, or sentences that touched you. In faith we expect God to speak to our soul through the Word and the Spirit.

meditatio.title: MEDITATIO – MEDITATION
meditatio.body:
This second step invites you to reflect on the Word—the words, phrases, and sentences that spoke to you—and let them come to the forefront.
Write them down and allow them to penetrate the depths of your heart. Repeat them again and again, considering the feelings or emotions they stir in you. Ask yourself: 'What is the Holy Spirit telling me through these words?' What do these words mean to me? What is God saying to my heart through them?
This part resembles Mary's response in Luke 2:51 where it says she kept all these words in her heart.

oratio.title: ORATIO – PRAYER
oratio.body:
Prayer according to God's Word (in your own words).
This step encourages a prayerful response. After re-reading and pondering the words, phrases, and sentences that touched you, and after asking the related questions, take these thoughts to heart and craft a prayer—your personal response to the Lord. Tell God what is on your heart; offer Him a prayer of love, gratitude, petition, or intercession. Sit quietly, write the prayer, draw a picture—just respond actively to the word you received.

contemplatio.title: CONTEMPLATIO – CONTEMPLATION
contemplatio.body:
An inner gaze of the heart at Jesus who steps out of the text; a look at Jesus whose characteristic you recognized while meditating on the text. This is the space to rest in God.
We become still and simply remain in God as His beloved. This is not easy and requires patience and discipline.
Stay for a moment in silence and allow the Lord to love you and to plant in your heart the words He has given you throughout this lectio divina process. This is prayer of presence, a movement from conversation to union.

actio.title: ACTIO – ACTION
actio.body: Formulate one short sentence that you will recall throughout the day.

practical.title: Reading the Bible with the "lectio divina" method – practically:
practical.body:
Preparatory step: Choose a short Bible text (a passage from the New Testament). Before you start reading the sacred text, invoke the Holy Spirit. Pray for His presence, become aware that He is with you, ask Him to reveal what is hidden in the text and to guide you. For example: Come, Holy Spirit. Enlighten my mind. Give me love for GOD'S WORD. Help me understand what GOD'S WORD wants to tell me. Help me listen carefully to your instructions.

Second step: Read GOD'S WORD (LECTIO)...
Third step: Meditate (MEDITATIO)...
Fourth step: Pray GOD'S WORD (ORATIO)...
Fifth step: Gaze at God's Word—at Jesus (CONTEMPLATIO)...
Sixth step: Live God's Word (ACTIO)...
Seventh step: Finish your encounter with GOD'S WORD with prayer, especially thanksgiving.

tips.title: What not to forget with this form of reading God's Word:
tips.body: MAKE TIME: Most of us do not have time to spare. This journal together with the app will help you find at least twenty minutes during the day to practice reading God's Word through Lectio divina. Make time! CREATE A SPACE: Truly find a place where you can enter the Lectio process. Jesus is the example—He found time to go to a particular place to spend time in prayer with the Father. PERSEVERE: This is a long-term project. It requires dedication and determination. Perseverance needs to be trained.

how.wish: I wish that time spent with Christ in this way becomes a time when you discover yourself, God's will, and the resolve to persevere in what is good.
